distinguishing_features: Feed-forward real-time modulation of ICCP anode current above the static -0.85 V vs Ag/AgCl setpoint, gated by electrolyte presence, rather than a constant conservative impressed potential

Uses the ratio of localized seawater conductivity to total system resistance to derive the instantaneous wetting phase and scale protection current to the oxygen-diffusion spike at the dry-to-wet transition
Wet/dry switching via a conductivity threshold (10 mS/cm) so protection is applied only when the electrolyte bridge exists, avoiding forced polarization during dry phases
Conductance derived from the existing ICCP current source by V_drop/I_known, requiring no new sensor hardware
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to avoid under-protection during the brief high-current wetting transient (thinned O2 diffusion layer) while avoiding over-protection/embrittlement and wasted energy during the long dry phase of the tidal cycle, using the existing ICCP anode hardware.
parsed.viable_reason: Modulating applied cathodic current proportional to electrolyte presence is physically wrong-signed for the stated problem: a thinned diffusion layer caps the O2 reduction current, so the required protection current drops during wetting rather than spiking, and gating current off when dry contradicts the goal of holding a protection potential at the aeration-cell onset, making the core mechanism implausible as written.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Feed-forward, conductivity-gated real-time current modulation decoupled from a fixed time/potential schedule is not the approach of any cited prior art (which are chloride pulse-dosing, molybdate inhibitor dosing, and impedance-based corrosion inference), so the modulation control scheme itself would not be an obvious step from that art.
